prompt: A monumental sculptural classic rubber duck as the singular centrepiece, positioned dead-centre in a 16:9 editorial frame. The duck body is finished in a deep charcoal near-black with a matte porcelain surface quality, identical in outline to the standard silhouette. It stands upright with no props, beak forward, feet planted, plain oval pupils (no decorative glint). The seamless backdrop is a saturated coral-red (#FF5544) — flat color field, no gradient, no texture. Soft directional window light enters from the upper left, wrapping the form with a gentle highlight along the crown and shoulder, while a soft fill on the right keeps the shadow side readable. A subtle ambient occlusion gathers at the feet but no cast shadow lands on the backdrop. Camera is straight-on, slightly elevated, 30 degrees, with the duck occupying roughly 60 percent of the frame height. The mood is editorial, confident, product-forward — a sculpture photographed for a magazine spread, restrained and centred. No accessories, no surface reflections, no off-tone cast anywhere in the frame.
